entries.title: About Kaizirege & Kemebos Schools (shule, overview, utangulizi)
entries.content: Kaizirege & Kemebos Schools is a group of boarding schools for boys and girls in Bukoba, Kagera Region, Tanzania. It runs three campuses: Primary (Kindergarten/PP up to Grade Seven), Secondary O-Level (Form One to Form Four) and High School A-Level (Form Five and Six), so a child can study from early childhood to Advanced Level in one school family. Motto: "Education for Outstanding Heights". The mother school is Kaizirege Primary School (officially Kaizirege English Medium Boarding Primary School) at Mtara, Ijuganyondo Ward, Bukoba Municipality. Kaizirege and Kemebos each have their own primary, secondary and high school with separate national results. Office hours: Monday to Saturday 08:00 - 18:00. The school describes itself as number 1 in national examinations, trusted by 5000+ clients, parents and students, with 50+ education awards. Shule ya bweni ya wavulana na wasichana, Bukoba, Kagera, Tanzania. Contacts are in the Contacts entry.

entries.title: History: how the school was founded (historia, mwanzilishi)
entries.content: Kaizirege Primary School was founded on 1 August 2007 and officially opened on 1 January 2008 by His Excellency Dr. Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete, the Fourth President of Tanzania. Construction began in 2006 and the first phase was finished by the end of 2007. It was founded by Mr. Eusto Kaizirege Ntagalinda (founder and Managing Director) whose dream was world-class education inside Tanzania, so fewer Tanzanian students would leave the country to study abroad. First management team: Mrs. Elizabeth Kaizirege (Deputy Director) and Mr. Elogius Katiti (Deputy School Manager). Founding technical staff: Headmaster Mr. Francis Muso, founding Academic Master Mr. Evans Kiziri, and teachers Edith Nababi, Medard Bwauika, A. Y. Kushaka and Azizi Komungoma. About 50 pupils were admitted in the first year, and it was a fully boarding school from the start. In 2008 the first examination class achieved outstanding results; in 2010 the first Primary Seven candidates ranked among the top schools in the country.

entries.title: History: growth, secondary, Kemebos and high school (ukuaji wa shule)
entries.content: Kaizirege Secondary School was established in 2011 for pupils finishing Primary Seven. Its first Form Two (FTNA) candidates ranked among the best in Tanzania, and the Managing Director began a tradition of rewarding outstanding students and teachers. In 2013 the pioneering Form Four class ranked first nationally among schools with fewer than forty candidates. As enrolment grew, Kemebos School and other campuses were added, and the High School (Advanced Level) campus began operations in 2016, giving a continuous path from early childhood to Form Six. The school celebrated its 19th anniversary on 1 August 2026 (founded 2007). Today: modern science laboratories (Physics, Chemistry, Biology), computer laboratories for ICT and Computer Studies, a dispensary, CCTV security cameras across the campuses, and school transport able to serve students from all regions of Tanzania (holidays, educational tours, field trips, picnics). Co-curricular: sports, debate clubs, scouting and leadership programmes. Many alumni study at universities in Tanzania and abroad.

entries.title: Mission, vision and motto (dira, dhamira, maono)
entries.content: Motto: "Education for Outstanding Heights". Mission (founding statement): to properly guide the coming generation on how to overcome the challenges of life in a dynamic world while respecting and preserving their African heritage, values and identity. Current mission statement: to provide high-quality, learner-centred education in a safe, inclusive and supportive environment that promotes academic excellence, discipline, integrity, creativity and leadership, with effective teaching, modern learning resources, practical experiences and strong moral values. Vision: to be a leading centre of excellence in education, recognised for nurturing academically outstanding, morally upright, innovative and responsible learners who succeed in a changing world and contribute to society. Three pillars: Knowledge (learners know what to do and what to avoid), Wisdom (ability to make sound decisions from knowledge and experience), Virtue (honesty, integrity, patriotism, loyalty and strong moral values).

entries.title: Core values of the school (maadili)
entries.content: The school is guided by nine core values: Excellence (highest standards in academics and all activities); Integrity (honesty, transparency, accountability); Discipline (self-control, responsibility, respect for school rules); Respect (valuing every individual, diversity and inclusion); Innovation (creativity, critical thinking, continuous improvement); Leadership (confident, responsible, service-oriented leaders); Teamwork (working together for common goals); Compassion (kindness, empathy and care); Responsibility (owning our actions and contributing to the community). Nidhamu, uadilifu, heshima, uongozi na ushirikiano ni sehemu ya maadili ya shule.

entries.title: Founders and directors (waanzilishi, mkurugenzi)
entries.content: Founder, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO): Mr. Eusto Kaizirege Ntagalinda, also called the School Director. Co-Director, CEO and Head of Accountancy: Mrs. Elizabeth Kaizirege Ntagalinda. The two founders are visionary educational leaders who believe every child deserves access to excellent education and set up the school to nurture academically successful, disciplined and morally responsible learners. The Director and Co-Director provide the overall vision and leadership: strategic planning, policy implementation, infrastructure development, financial management and continuous improvement. Contacts: Director +255 677 848 343 / +255 744 759 886, eustokaizirege@gmail.com; Accountancy office +255 755 760 268 / +255 716 298 280.

entries.title: School Board, headmasters and academic masters (uongozi, bodi ya shule)
entries.content: School Board: Chairman Mr. Kagasheki; Assistant Chairman Mr. Bina. The Board gives strategic guidance and oversight. Headmaster: Mr. Kisha Ilamulila (phone +255 714 795 465), named as the High School (Advanced Level) Headmaster and listed first among the school's Headmasters. Academic masters: Primary campus - Mr. Ssemanda Joseph and Mr. Patience Ignatus (also written Tr./Mwl.); Secondary campus - Mwl. Bajanda Ndagala and Mwl. Jackson Robert Minja. Academic masters coordinate curriculum, examinations, lesson planning, continuous assessment and monitoring of progress. Also: heads of departments, qualified teaching staff, and non-teaching staff (administrators, accountants, librarians, lab technicians, ICT staff, matrons and patrons, nurses, cooks, drivers, security, cleaners, gardeners, maintenance). Founding staff: Mr. Francis Muso (first Headmaster), Mr. Evans Kiziri (founding Academic Master, Head of English Department, longest-serving staff member), Edith Nababi, Medard Bwauika, A. Y. Kushaka, Azizi Komungoma.

entries.content: The schools welcome passionate, qualified and committed professionals: educators, and people in administration, support services and other school operations. entries.title: Admissions 2026: Primary (PP to Primary Six) and how to get the joining form (udahili, fomu ya kujiunga)
entries.content: Admissions are open for academic year 2026/27 in the non-candidate primary classes: PP (Pre-Primary), P1, P2, P3, P5 and P6 (Udahili unaendelea: PP/Awali, Darasa la Kwanza, la Pili, la Tatu, la Tano na la Sita). Steps (hatua za kujiunga): 1) Application: buy the joining form (fomu ya kujiunga) at the school campus, the Dar es Salaam office or the Dodoma office (online platform still being built); 2) Interview (usaili) to confirm the place; 3) Payment of fees and the admission fee via bank; 4) Enrollment (kujiunga): the student starts; 5) Orientation: meet staff and students. Required: completed application form, identification documents, admission fee payment receipt. Form + interview TSh 60,000 (also for PP-P1). Contact +255 677 848 343, +255 755 760 268, info@kaiziregekemebos.sc.tz. A student who has not completed the required payments will not be received at school.

entries.title: Admissions 2026: Secondary O-Level and the Pre-Form One Course (udahili sekondari, Pre-Form One)
entries.content: Secondary school admission interviews (usaili) are running for the non-candidate classes: Form One (F1) and Form Three (F3). Kidato cha Kwanza na Kidato cha Tatu. Pre-Form One Course 2026: a short bridging programme from primary to secondary that revises primary concepts, builds study habits, independence, discipline, confidence and time management, and introduces secondary school life. Duration: 1 October 2026 to 20 December 2026 (1 Oktoba - 20 Desemba 2026). Pre-Form One interviews started on 19 September 2026; a second round was announced for 23 September 2026. Joining Form: collect it at the school campus, the Dar es Salaam office or the Dodoma office (online platform still being built). Contact +255 677 848 343 or +255 755 760 268. Fees are in the Secondary fee entries.

entries.title: Admissions 2026/27: High School Form Five and Form Six, new PMC combination (udahili kidato cha tano na sita)
entries.content: Applications are open for Form Five and Form Six students joining academic year 2026/2027 (Udahili wa Kidato cha Tano na Kidato cha Sita, mwaka wa masomo 2026/2027). New programme: the PMC combination (Physics, Mathematics and Computer Science/Computer Studies) for careers in science, technology, engineering and computing, announced 10 July 2026. Joining Form: collect it at the school campus, the Dar es Salaam office or the Dodoma office; an online platform is being developed. Contact +255 677 848 343 or +255 755 760 268. Fee structure (mchanganuo wa ada) is in the High School fee entries; Form Five 2026/2027 is paid in two terms (Jul-Dec 2026 and Jan-Jun 2027).

entries.title: Fees 2026 Primary PP to P1: school fees, terms, installments (ada ya shule ya msingi PP-P1)
entries.content: PP-P1 annual fees 2026: school fees (karo ya shule) TSh 1,900,000; medical treatment (matibabu) TSh 100,000 per year; total TSh 2,000,000. Paper (karatasi): TSh 17,000 per ream, one ream each term (2 reams a year). Payable in two terms (mihula miwili) of TSh 1,000,000 each, or in four installments (awamu nne), each TSh 500,000: installment 1 is due in January, installment 2 in April, installment 3 in July, installment 4 in September; total TSh 2,000,000. New PP-P1 student, first installment: the joining form states TSh 997,000 (this includes the 500,000 first installment, admission fee 130,000, uniform 350,000 and paper 17,000). Admission fee TSh 130,000 is paid once per new student. Form + interview TSh 60,000. Uniform prices and bank accounts are in separate entries.

entries.title: Fees 2026 Primary P2 to P7: school fees, terms, installments (ada ya shule ya msingi P2-P7)
entries.content: P2-P7 annual fees 2026: school fees (karo ya shule) TSh 2,300,000; medical treatment (matibabu) TSh 100,000 per year; total TSh 2,400,000. Paper (karatasi): TSh 17,000 per ream, one ream each term. Payable in two terms (mihula miwili) of TSh 1,200,000 each, or four installments (awamu nne), each TSh 600,000: installment 1 is due in January, installment 2 in April, installment 3 in July, installment 4 in September; total TSh 2,400,000. New student, first installment: the joining form states TSh 1,097,000 (600,000 first installment + admission fee 130,000 + uniform 350,000 + paper 17,000). Admission fee TSh 130,000 is paid once per new student. Form + interview TSh 60,000. Student must have fully paid the required fees, otherwise not received at school.

entries.title: Primary school uniform prices 2026 (sare za shule ya msingi)
entries.content: Complete primary school uniform (sare za shule) costs TSh 350,000 in total: classroom uniform 2 pairs TSh 80,000; outside-class uniform 2 pairs TSh 80,000; worship-day (ibada) uniform 1 pair TSh 40,000; tracksuit and T-shirt TSh 70,000; socks 2 pairs TSh 20,000; sweaters 2 TSh 60,000. This applies to both PP-P1 and P2-P7 new students. Summary of primary fees 2026 (PP-P1 | P2-P7): school fees 1,900,000 | 2,300,000; medical 100,000 | 100,000; total 2,000,000 | 2,400,000; per term 1,000,000 | 1,200,000; four installments 500,000 x4 | 600,000 x4; admission 130,000 | 130,000; form + interview 60,000 | 60,000; uniform 350,000 | 350,000; paper 17,000 | 17,000.

entries.content: Primary school fees and all other payments must be paid into the school's bank accounts (malipo yote kupitia benki): CRDB Bank 01J1056588101; NMB 31806600128; NBC 027103003745; Tanzania Commercial Bank 230207000029. A student who has not fully paid the required fees will not be received at school. Note: Secondary and High School use a different set of accounts (see the Secondary and High School payment entry).

entries.title: Fees 2026 Secondary Form One to Form Four: school fees and installments (ada ya sekondari)
entries.content: Secondary (Form One to Form Four) 2026: total annual school fees (jumla ya ada kwa mwaka) TSh 4,100,000, payable in four equal installments (awamu nne) of TSh 1,025,000: January, April, July and September. Medical fee (matibabu) TSh 100,000 per year. Paper ream (rimu ya karatasi) TSh 17,000 in January and TSh 17,000 in July. New (first-time) student first payment: admission fee (ada ya kujiandikisha) TSh 150,000; first-term fee TSh 1,000,000; school uniform (sare) TSh 410,000; medical TSh 25,000; identity card (kitambulisho) TSh 10,000; paper ream TSh 17,000. entries.title: Secondary school uniform prices 2026 (sare za sekondari)
entries.content: Complete secondary school uniform, all students: classroom uniform 2 pairs TSh 100,000; worship-day (ibada) uniform 1 pair TSh 50,000; outside-class uniform 2 pairs TSh 100,000; tracksuit + T-shirt 1 set TSh 70,000; socks 2 pairs TSh 20,000; sweaters 2 TSh 60,000; tie 1 TSh 10,000. entries.title: Fees Form Five 2026/2027: Business and Arts combinations (ada kidato cha tano, mchepuo wa biashara na sanaa)
entries.content: Form Five 2026/2027, Business and Arts combinations (EGM, HKL, HGE, HGL, HGK and EBuAc / EB/AC): school fees TSh 5,000,000 per year; medical (matibabu) TSh 100,000; total TSh 5,100,000 per year. entries.title: Fees Form Five 2026/2027: Science combinations (ada kidato cha tano, mchepuo wa sayansi)

Paid in two terms: Term One (Jul-Dec 2026) TSh 2,900,000 (fees 2,750,000 + medical 50,000 + laboratory 100,000); Term Two (Jan-Jun 2027) TSh 2,900,000 (fees 2,750,000 + medical 50,000 + laboratory 100,000). Ada ya mchepuo wa sayansi: Tsh 5,800,000 kwa mwaka.

entries.title: New Form Five / Form Six students: extra payments and uniform (malipo ya mwanafunzi mpya)
entries.content: A student joining Form Five or Form Six for the first time pays the fees for their combination plus: admission fee (usajili), paid once, TSh 200,000; identity card TSh 10,000; one ream of paper per term TSh 17,000; complete school uniform TSh 410,000. entries.title: Bank accounts for Secondary and High School fees (akaunti za benki sekondari na high school)
entries.content: Secondary (Form One to Four) and High School (Form Five and Six) fees are paid through the bank. The High School account name is KAIZIREGE BOARDING HIGH SCHOOL. Accounts: NMB 31806600311; CRDB Bank 0150225212600; NBC 027103003733; Tanzania Commercial Bank 230207000005. Write the student's name on the bank pay-in slip and bring the ORIGINAL slip to school to receive the official receipt. Students must complete the required payments before being received at school. Primary school uses different accounts (see the Primary payment entry).

entries.title: Primary campus: pupils, facilities and curriculum (shule ya msingi, kampasi ya msingi)
entries.content: The Primary campus is for pupils from Kindergarten to Grade Seven (the subjects page says Kindergarten to Grade Six under the new curriculum). It has spacious classrooms, a library, computer facilities, playgrounds, and nutritious meals; boarding for boys and girls is supervised by matrons and patrons. Subjects: English Language, Kiswahili, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, Civic and Moral Education, ICT, Creative Arts, Physical Education and Life Skills. Kindergarten learns through play: language and communication, early literacy and numeracy, creative arts, physical, social and emotional development. Activities: sports, music, arts, clubs, educational events. Academic masters: Ssemanda Joseph and Patience Ignatus.

entries.title: New primary curriculum: candidate classes Grade 4, 6 and 7 (mtaala mpya, darasa la sita)
entries.content: Under the new national curriculum, Grade Six becomes the final candidate class for the Primary School Leaving Assessment, replacing the former Grade Seven examination. The school will have three candidate classes: Grade 4, Grade 6 and Grade 7, each with focused preparation for its national assessment. Teaching uses continuous assessment and competency-based learning. Darasa la Sita sasa ni darasa la mwisho la mtihani wa kuhitimu elimu ya msingi; madarasa ya mitihani ni la nne, la sita na la saba.

entries.title: Secondary campus (O-Level, Form One to Four): subjects and facilities (kampasi ya sekondari)
entries.content: The Secondary campus offers a balanced curriculum with modern classrooms, science laboratories, computer laboratories, a well-stocked library and sports facilities (football ground). Ordinary Level (Forms I-IV) subjects examined by NECTA: Mathematics, English Language, Kiswahili, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, History, Geography, Civics, Business Studies, and Historia ya Tanzania na Maadili. Many students achieve Division I and II in Form Two and Form Four results. Activities: sports, debate, music and arts. Learning is interactive: group work, practicals, presentations and digital tools, with regular assessments and feedback. Academic masters: Mwl. Bajanda Ndagala and Mwl. Jackson Robert Minja. Boarding is described in the boarding entry.

entries.title: High School campus (A-Level, Form Five and Six): subject combinations (tahasusi, mchepuo)
entries.content: The High School (Advanced Level) prepares Form Five and Form Six for ACSEE and university. Science combinations: PCB (Physics, Chemistry, Biology); PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Advanced Mathematics); PGM (Physics, Geography, Advanced Mathematics); CBG (Chemistry, Biology, Geography); and the new PMC (Physics, Mathematics, Computer Studies). Business: EB/AC (Economics, Business Studies, Accountancy / Accountancy, Commerce, Economics; also written EBuAc). Arts and social sciences: EGM (Economics, Geography, Advanced Mathematics), HGK (History, Geography, Kiswahili), HKL (History, Kiswahili, English Language), HGE (History, Geography, Economics), HGL (History, Geography, English Language). General Studies is compulsory for all. Pages differ on EGM: listed under Science on one page, under Arts/Business elsewhere. The fee structure puts EGM with Business and Arts.

entries.title: High School learning: laboratories, assessment, Headmaster (maabara, ACSEE)
entries.content: High School learning is aligned with the national curriculum with class exercises, assignments, tests, projects and mock examinations leading to ACSEE. Science students do regular practicals in well-equipped Physics, Chemistry and Biology laboratories; there are also computer facilities, a library and study spaces. Students join sports, clubs, debates, leadership programmes and community service. Career guidance targets medicine, engineering, education, business, law, IT and social sciences. Headmaster: Mr. Kisha Ilamulila. Form Six 2026 graduation was held on 25 April 2026 with 212 students.

entries.title: Boarding, food, dormitories and sports (bweni, chakula, michezo)
entries.content: All three campuses offer boarding for both boys and girls with experienced matrons, patrons and boarding staff, structured study time (evening preparation/prep), recreation and rest. Meals: balanced, nutritious breakfast, lunch and dinner prepared in a clean, hygienic kitchen; fresh drinking water is available. Dormitories are clean, safe, well ventilated and supervised. Sports: football, netball, volleyball, basketball, athletics and other indoor and outdoor games, with inter-house competitions and friendly matches. Other activities: music, arts, debate, scouting, clubs and leadership programmes. CCTV cameras cover the campuses for security. The school also runs transport for holidays, tours, field trips and picnics.

entries.title: Health department and school dispensary (zahanati, afya, matibabu)
entries.content: The school has a modern dispensary run by qualified medical personnel. Services: first aid, routine care, health assessments, emergency response and basic treatment for students and staff, with male and female observation rooms, a laboratory and a pharmacy. The Health Department monitors students' health, gives health education and works with parents and healthcare providers; parents are informed when necessary. Matrons, patrons, teachers and the medical team monitor student well-being together. Fees include an annual medical charge (matibabu) of TSh 100,000 for Primary, Secondary and High School.

entries.title: School departments (idara za shule)
entries.content: Departments: Academic, Science, Mathematics, Languages, Humanities, ICT, Examinations, Boarding, Sports and Co-curricular Activities, Administration and Finance, Transport, and Health and Welfare. The Academic Department coordinates curriculum, lesson planning, examinations, assessments, performance monitoring and teacher support. The Science Department covers classroom learning, laboratory practicals, research and experiments, preparing learners for medicine, engineering, technology and other science careers. Head of English Department: Mr. Evans Kiziri. Accountancy Office: Mrs. Elizabeth Kaizirege Ntagalinda, +255 755 760 268.

entries.title: School bus service and public Dar es Salaam - Bukoba buses (basi, usafiri)
entries.content: Kaizirege & Kemebos Bus Services provides (1) school transport between home and school on designated routes with experienced drivers, for holidays, tours, field trips and picnics, able to serve students from all regions of Tanzania; and (2) public passenger buses across Tanzania. A daily VIP bus service and a semi-luxury service run between Dar es Salaam and Bukoba (both directions). Fares, timetable and phone numbers are in the bus fares entry. Book online at kaiziregekemebos.co.tz. Usafiri wa kila siku Dar es Salaam - Bukoba; weka nafasi mtandaoni.

entries.title: News September 2026: graduation date and national exam dates (taarifa, mahafali, NECTA)
entries.content: As of 29 September 2026: the Primary Seven (P7) and Form Four (F4) Graduation Ceremony has moved to 17 October 2026; parents and guardians are welcome. NECTA revised 2026 exam dates (heavy rain concerns): Standard Four SFNA 5-6 October 2026 (was 21-22 October); Standard Two STNA 7-8 October 2026 (was 17-18 November); Form Two FTNA 12-23 October 2026 (was 2-13 November); Form Four CSEE 19 October - 6 November 2026 (was 9-27 November). Academic Excellence Award celebrated 29 September 2026. Pre-Form One interviews began 19 September 2026, second round 23 September 2026; the Pre-Form One course runs 1 October - 20 December 2026.

entries.title: News and events: April to August 2026
entries.content: 1 August 2026: 19th anniversary celebration. 29 August 2026: picnic and best wishes to Primary Four (P4) and Primary Seven (P7) pupils before their examinations. 10 July 2026: Computer Studies and the new PMC combination introduced at A-Level. 6 July 2026: Form Six (ACSEE) 2026 results released, with congratulations to the class of 2026. 25 April 2026: Form Six Graduation Ceremony for 212 students, attended by ELCT Bishop Dr. Alex Malasusa and government leaders.

Phones: Bukoba Mjini +255 680 996 195; Shekilango Dar es Salaam +255 712 980 557. Booking: kaiziregekemebos.co.tz.

entries.title: Awards: national honours (tuzo za taifa, NECTA, Tanzania National Academic Awards)
entries.content: Kemebos was named best school in Tanzania (shule bora ya kwanza kitaifa) in the 2019 CSEE and second best in the 2020 ACSEE, with NECTA academic quality certificates dated 22 October 2020. At the Tanzania National Academic Awards (President's Office, Regional Administration and Local Government): Kemebos - Kagera 1st in the Top 10 overall CSEE 2019 and 2nd in the Top 10 overall ACSEE 2020 (awarded 22 October 2020 by the Minister of State, Hon. Selemani S. Jafo); 10th in the Top 10 overall ACSEE 2019 (October 2019); 2nd in the Top 10 overall best performed schools ACSEE 2021; a 4th-place trophy for Kemebos Primary (PSLE 2021). Ministry of Education certificates of commendation: Kemebos Secondary best performing non-government secondary school in CSEE 2018 (awarded 14 June 2019) and CSEE 2019; Kemebos Primary best performing non-government primary school in PSLE 2019; Kemebos Secondary best performing secondary school CSEE 2017.

entries.title: Awards: Kaizirege honours from the Ministry and the President (tuzo za Kaizirege)
entries.content: Kaizirege Primary School: Government Certificates of Commendation as one of the Best Performing Schools in PSLE 2013 (awarded 10 May 2014), best performing non-government primary school in PSLE 2015 (awarded June 2016) and PSLE 2016 (awarded 12 June 2017), plus trophies for best performing PSLE 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016. Kaizirege Secondary School: appreciation awards from President Jakaya Kikwete as best performing non-government secondary school in CSEE 2013 (May 2014) and CSEE 2014 (May 2015), a Ministry certificate for CSEE 2015 (awarded June 2016), the trophy for Most Improved Non-Government School in CSEE 2013 and Most Improved Secondary School CSEE 2019. Bukoba Municipality gave the first place among non-government schools in the primary leaving exam 2013 and first place among private secondary schools in Form Four 2013. Kaizirege Primary was also among the top ten schools in Kagera Region in PSLE 2017.

entries.title: Awards: Bukoba Municipal Council, tax and community recognition (vyeti vya pongezi, Manispaa ya Bukoba)

entries.title: School calendar 2026: holidays, opening and closing dates (kalenda, likizo, kufunga shule)
entries.content: Closing for the September holidays: Friday 4 September 2026 (non-candidate students). Reopening: Monday 14 September 2026. Graduation of P7 and F4: 17 October 2026. National exams: SFNA 5-6 Oct, STNA 7-8 Oct, FTNA 12-23 Oct, CSEE 19 Oct - 6 Nov 2026. Pre-Form One course 1 Oct - 20 Dec 2026. entries.title: Pre-Form One 2026 interview centres and time (vituo vya usaili, Pre Form One)
entries.content: Pre-Form One 2026 admission interviews were announced for Saturday 19 September 2026 at 1:30 asubuhi (7:30 in the morning), "Karibu uwe sehemu ya safari ya mafanikio". Interview centres (vituo vya usaili): Bukoba-Kagera at the school (Kaizirege & Kemebos); Dar es Salaam - Kinondoni at the school offices near Kinondoni Studio, Livingstone street; Mwanza at Mwanza Secondary School; Dodoma at the school offices at Machinga Complex roundabout on the Iringa road, opposite the ORYX petrol station; Arusha at Meru Primary School in Arusha city, opposite Kaloleni hospital near St. Thereza church and the main police station. A second round took place on 23 September 2026. Contact: Head Master +255 714 795 465; School Director +255 677 848 343; Assistant Director +255 755 760 268.

entries.title: Admission process P2 to P7: requirements and extra costs (kujiunga na shule P2-P7)
entries.content: Joining Primary P2-P7 (from the school's admission guide of 27 August 2026): key requirements are the joining fee, a one-time admission interview, and school fees; all new students sit an admission interview before making further payments. Steps: Application (buy required forms), Interview, Payment, Enrollment (officially join the school), Orientation (meet staff and students). Annual fee TSh 2,400,000 in 4 installments; additional fees total TSh 614,000: medical TSh 100,000, uniforms TSh 350,000, two paper reams TSh 34,000, plus the admission fee TSh 130,000. Prepare payment details (joining fee payment, admission fee payment) and schedule your interview by choosing a date and confirming attendance. Contact +255 677 848 343, info@kaiziregekemebos.sc.tz.
